items.article: From checking blood sugar to looking for signs of inflammation, lab reports provide useful clues about what is happening inside your body. A blood test can tell you much more about your health than you may realise. From checking blood sugar to looking for signs of inflammation, lab reports provide useful clues about what is happening inside your body. But with so many numbers and medical terms on a report, it can be difficult to know which results deserve attention. Nutritionist Nmami Agarwal highlights five health markers that people may want to understand when looking at their reports. These include HbA1c, LDL and triglycerides, ferritin, fasting insulin and HOMA-IR, and hs-CRP. On Instagram, Agarwal explains that HbA1c shows the average blood sugar level over the past three months, rather than showing only one day's reading. LDL and triglycerides are part of a cholesterol test. LDL is one type of cholesterol, while triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood. Their levels can provide information about how the body handles fats and extra calories. Ferritin tells you about the iron stored in the body. A low ferritin level can mean that your iron stores are low, even if your hemoglobin looks normal. Fasting insulin and HOMA-IR can provide information about how the body uses insulin and may help identify insulin resistance early. HS-CRP, on the other hand, is a blood marker linked to inflammation in the body. Doctors may also look at this result with other health information

items.text: Work Email Missing on Your Mac? This Could Be Why
items.article: If your work email on your Mac isn't syncing today, it might well have to do with Microsoft's cut-off of Exchange Web Services (EWS). As of October 1, 2026, Microsoft began switching off EWS by default in Exchange Online. If you haven't heard of it before, EWS is the aging protocol that Apple's Mail and Calendar apps still use to sync Microsoft 365 work accounts. The cutoff has been signposted for a while. Microsoft stopped adding new features to EWS back in 2018, while in 2023 the company announced that it would start disabling the protocol in Exchange Online from October 2026. It's being described as a phased rollout, so some users may be impacted sooner than others. For those affected, system admins can still turn EWS back on, but only until April 1, 2027, when it shuts down for good. Apple says that it is "actively working with Microsoft" to move its Mac apps over to the newer Graph API in a macOS 27 update. That update has yet to arrive, but it surely won't be long before it does. In the meantime, Outlook for Mac works just fine, and iPhone and iPad users won't be affected because they use Exchange ActiveSync rather than EWS. Get weekly top MacRumors stories in your inbox.

This is in addition to the one small personal bag that must fit under the seat in front of the passenger or have maximum dimensions of 40 x 30 x 15cm. The 90-foot arch at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park on the Big Island was standing firm Wednesday, Sept. 23, but was gone by Sunday night, according to the National Park Service . Officials do not know exactly when the tourist attraction fell and suspect it may have happened while the park was temporarily closed for three days during Tropical Storm Nolo . items.article: O'Connell's Irish pub is the home of many iconic intimate gigs Pop star Tom Grennan will be performing in one of Manchester's most popular Irish bar as he is set to play his new acoustic set for fans. Tickets are free, but those wanting to go to the intimate gig are urged to hurry. The singer will take to the stage at O’Connell’s next Wednesday (October 7) for a special live performance, with organisers promising fans a rare chance to see the chart-topping artist in a much smaller setting. Before it became O'Connell's in early 2025, the historic venue tucked beneath the railway arches of Oxford Road train station was known for decades as The Thirsty Scholar. It was also where Tom played one of his very first gigs, Announcing the show on social media, O’Connell’s said: “Join us next Wednesday for an intimate acoustic gig from @tom.grennan – who’s revisiting us after he played one of his first ever gigs here!” The appearance will be a homecoming of sorts for Grennan, who previously performed at the venue during the early stages of his career. Tickets for the intimate gig will be free, but numbers are expected to be extremely limited. O’Connell’s urged fans not to miss the opportunity, adding: “Tickets are free, but very very limited! items.article: Sad to part ways with your above-limit expensive shampoo or nail scissors? Here's what really happens to your confiscated items... Published: 12:08, 2 October 2026 | Updated: 12:12, 2 October 2026 We all know that frustrating moment when, after sailing through security at the airport, your bag is hauled aside for an extra check. Whether it's a pair of nail scissors, a razor or an extra power bank that has you receiving that oh-so-judgemental look from security personnel, it's always frustrating to have your belongings confiscated before jetting off on holiday. But what actually happens to your items once they've been confiscated? Earlier this year, Manchester Airport showcased a selection of items its security officers were forced to confiscate in the space of just one morning. Among almost 100 items removed from bags in Terminal 2 security in July were 24 packs of cosmetic products, seven drinks bottles and seven food items – including two multipacks of yoghurts.
